rationale: Evidence: 60 development trials across iterations 0, 2, 3 and 4 gave 2 finishes, both on the oval at base_speed 1.0. The best design so far (iteration 4, score 129.05) moved the sensors forward to y=0.07 with a +/-0.05 m span. That raised s-bend progress to 0.156 and slalom progress to 0.10, against 0.04 and 0.035 at y=0.04, so forward sensing is the change that has helped. Speed (0.9 to 1.6) and gains (kp 2 to 4) did not move the failure point, so the limit appears to be how early the robot sees the line. Iteration 5 was never raced, so its seven-sensor layout has no evidence. Change: move the sensors to y=0.08, the contract maximum, so the correction starts about 1 cm earlier than in iteration 4. Keep the proven 5-sensor layout at +/-0.05 m, with 16 mm footprints and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. Keep kp 4.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.6 and base_speed 1.0, since these were the settings that produced the two oval finishes. Wheel track, radius, body and mass are unchanged. Expected result: progress above 0.16 on the s-bend and slalom, and more oval completions than 2 of 20. The change is small, so a large gain is not expected; if the robot still exits at the same point, the next race should point to the line-loss handling or the kd term.
